content:
Requirement R09 (input): Initiate Takeover Request. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to request control takeover of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-09.1, F-09.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-09.<F>.1, Be-09.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-09.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Allow the pilot to request control takeover of a UAV currently managed by a UAV Pilot — the outbound request act (UC 4.1.1), not the subsequent connection/command procedure.

**Function candidates:**

**F-09.1 — Enable the pilot to issue a UAV takeover request.**
The artefact's purpose is to convert the pilot's intent into a transmittable takeover request directed at a target UAV. Pure origination: identify which UAV, express "request control." Effect measured by: a valid, correctly-addressed request reaches the aircraft for forwarding.

**F-09.2 — Enable the pilot to select/target which UAV to take over before requesting.**
Purpose is disambiguation: from a set of teamed UAVs, designate the correct one as the takeover target. This opens a different goal — target selection — that F-09.1 assumes as already resolved. Relevant if multiple UAVs are in play.

**F-09.3 — Enable the pilot to guard against erroneous takeover requests.**
Purpose is integrity: ensure a takeover request is deliberate, since it interrupts another operator's control authority. Effect measured by: no unintended request is transmitted (validation/deliberateness gate).

**My recommendation:** F-09.1 is the core requirement. F-09.2 (target selection) is realistically a prerequisite sub-goal that could either fold into F-09.1's behaviour or be its own function — flag: if multi-UAV targeting is handled generally, F-09.2's behaviour/structure will likely be **shared** with R10 (handover) and the UAV-control requirements (R05-family selection), not exclusive to R09. F-09.3 is a validation concern that echoes the "deliberate action" gate pattern from R03/R04/R05 and would reuse that framework.

Suggest closing on **F-09.1** as the primary, treating targeting as part of its behaviour. Agree, or do you want F-09.2 split out as its own function?

Closing Function on **F-09.1** and **F-09.3**.

Per instructions I carry one F index forward for the Behaviour/Structure layers. F-09.1 (issue the request) is the primary act; F-09.3 (guard against erroneous requests) is a validation gate that, as flagged, reuses the deliberate-action pattern from R03/R04/R05.

Two ways to proceed:
- **(a)** Treat F-09.3 as folded into F-09.1's behaviour (the request act *includes* its confirm/guard step) — one behaviour set covers both.
- **(b)** Run the Behaviour layer twice, once per function, keeping them formally separate.

I recommend **(a)**: the guard has no meaning independent of the request it protects, and splitting would just duplicate the same confirm structure. I'll design Be-09.1.x for the request act with the deliberateness gate embedded, and note explicitly where the gate satisfies F-09.3.

Confirm (a) or (b), then I'll propose behaviours.

**Behaviour candidates for F-09.1 (issue UAV takeover request, with embedded F-09.3 deliberateness gate). Fixed modalities: Touch, Keyboard.**

Assumed target selection resolved upstream (per F-09.1 scope) — but see shared-flag note below.

**Be-09.1.1 — Touch-only pathway.**
Pilot taps the target UAV on a takeover panel/roster, taps a REQUEST TAKEOVER control; a confirm affordance appears (distinct second tap = the F-09.3 gate) before the request is committed and handed to the aircraft. Measurable: request transmitted only after two deliberate touch events on distinct affordances; no single accidental tap fires it.

**Be-09.1.2 — Keyboard-only pathway.**
Pilot selects target UAV via bezel OSS / rotary step (cycle roster) and issues REQUEST via a dedicated OSS; the gate is a second discrete press (e.g. OSS-hold or a CONFIRM OSS) before commit. UCP alphanumeric can key a UAV ID directly as an alternate select. Measurable: full request completable with zero touch input; commit requires two distinct discrete actuations.

**Be-09.1.3 — Mixed pathway.**
Pilot touch-selects the UAV, then confirms via bezel CONFIRM OSS (or vice versa: OSS-cycle select, touch-confirm). Adds real value here: select-by-touch is fast when the roster is visible, while a physical CONFIRM OSS gives a positive-feel deliberate commit under vibration/glove conditions — better ergonomic fit for the gate than an on-glass confirm. Measurable: request commits on any select-then-confirm cross-modality sequence; either modality can serve either sub-step (satisfies the redundancy rule).

**Notes:**
- The F-09.3 gate = the second/confirm actuation in all three. Same press-and-confirm pattern as R03/R04/R05 — reuse, not new.
- **Shared flag:** the target-UAV selection sub-behaviour (roster select by touch or OSS/rotary) is almost certainly **shared with R10 handover** and any per-UAV addressing requirement. I'd design the selection widget once and reuse; R09 adds only the REQUEST+gate on top.

Recommend keeping all three (they satisfy modality-complete redundancy together). Which do you want to carry forward — or all three?
Keep all three, the confirmation system should be the same as before, and R10 is only the second part of this requirement. R09 requests it, and R10 is after the request is accepted.

Noted:
- All three behaviours kept: **Be-09.1.1** (Touch-only), **Be-09.1.2** (Keyboard-only), **Be-09.1.3** (Mixed).
- F-09.3 gate = the **same confirmation system as R03/R04/R05** (dual-input press-and-confirm), reused — not a new gate.
- **R09 = request** (this requirement); **R10 = after acceptance** (takeover execution/connection per UC 4.2). So R10 is *not* the handover — correcting my earlier note. The target-UAV selection widget is still plausibly shared between R09's request and R10's execution addressing, but that's a downstream consolidation, not designed here.

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI elements on fixed hardware, 2-3 sets per behaviour.

---

**S sets for Be-09.1.1 (Touch-only):**

**S-09.1.1.1 — Takeover panel with inline roster.**
New WAD overlay panel listing teamed UAVs (tail/ID, controlling operator, status). Each row touch-selectable; selected row highlights. A REQUEST TAKEOVER button in the panel footer; tapping raises the reused R03/R04/R05 confirm affordance (CONFIRM/CANCEL). Commit hands request to aircraft.

**S-09.1.1.2 — Map-integrated selection.**
Reuse existing **Map view**: UAV icons are touch targets; tapping one opens a context callout with a REQUEST TAKEOVER action → reused confirm. No separate roster panel. Better spatial SA (pilot sees where the UAV is) but weaker when icons overlap/off-screen.

---

**S sets for Be-09.1.2 (Keyboard-only):**

**S-09.1.2.1 — Bezel-driven roster.**
Same takeover panel (S-09.1.1.1 roster), but selection by **rotary knob** (cycle rows) and a bezel **REQUEST OSS**; confirm via the reused CONFIRM OSS. UCP alphanumeric as alternate direct-ID entry.

---

**S sets for Be-09.1.3 (Mixed):**

**S-09.1.3.1 — Shared takeover panel, both input rails live.**
The **single** takeover panel from S-09.1.1.1 with roster touch-select AND rotary-select both active, REQUEST available as both a touch button and a bezel OSS, confirm via the reused dual-input confirm control. This one structure physically satisfies all three behaviours + the redundancy rule.

---

**Recommendation:** Converge on **S-09.1.3.1** as the primary — one takeover panel that serves Be-09.1.1/.2/.3 simultaneously (no per-modality duplication), with **S-09.1.1.2** (map-integrated select) offered as a complementary alternate entry point if you want spatial selection. Everything reuses the R03/R04/R05 confirm.

Pick the structure(s) to close on.

**R09 closed.**

- **Function:** F-09.1 (issue UAV takeover request) with F-09.3 (deliberateness gate) folded in.
- **Behaviour:** Be-09.1.1 (Touch-only), Be-09.1.2 (Keyboard-only), Be-09.1.3 (Mixed) — all retained; F-09.3 gate realized as the reused R03/R04/R05 press-and-confirm.
- **Structure:** S-09.1.3.1 — single WAD takeover panel with roster, both input rails live (touch-select + rotary/OSS-select, REQUEST as touch button and bezel OSS), commit via reused dual-input confirm control.

**Carry-forward flags:**
- Confirm system = R03/R04/R05 reuse (no new gate).
- Target-UAV selection/roster likely shared with R10 (takeover execution addressing) — consolidate downstream.
- R10 = post-acceptance takeover execution (UC 4.2), not handover.

Ready for R10 when you are.
